citation.title: Consequences on islet and incretin hormone responses to dinner by omission of lunch in healthy men

population.description: Twelve lean healthy male volunteers aged 20-30 years (22.9 +/- 1.9 SD) with BMI 20-25 kg/m2 (22.5 +/- 1.5); the ranges are enrolment criteria. No personal history of diabetes or gastrointestinal disease, no medication.

protocols.name: dinner_after_lunch
protocols.description: Breakfast 08:00, lunch 13:00, dinner 17:00, sampled for 300 min after dinner. Grams derived as kcal x fraction / 4 (carbohydrate, protein) or / 9 (fat) from the printed energy and percentages: breakfast 524 kcal (19% protein, 18% fat, 63% carbohydrate) at 08:00; lunch 606 kcal (25% protein, 38% fat, 37% carbohydrate) at 13:00; dinner 690 kcal (25% protein, 35% fat, 40% carbohydrate) at 17:00. Overnight fast with no food after 22:00 to the 08:00 breakfast, 10 h.

protocols.name: dinner_no_lunch
protocols.description: Breakfast 08:00, no lunch, dinner 17:00, sampled for 300 min after dinner. Grams derived as kcal x fraction / 4 (carbohydrate, protein) or / 9 (fat) from the printed energy and percentages: breakfast 524 kcal (19% protein, 18% fat, 63% carbohydrate) at 08:00; dinner 690 kcal (25% protein, 35% fat, 40% carbohydrate) at 17:00. Overnight fast with no food after 22:00 to the 08:00 breakfast, 10 h.

findings.description: Suprabasal (incremental) area under the glucose curve after dinner, early 0-30 min, breakfast and lunch before the dinner. Table 1, mean of 12 men, SEM. The paper does not print when its two baseline samples were drawn, nor what lies under baseline; baseline taken as the value at the minute the dinner is given. The early and the late area add to 241.8 against a printed total of 243 ± 35 for this arm: a unit in the last digit, entered as printed.
